title: Costa Rica: Turtle & Wildlife Conservation
description: Protect endangered sea turtles along Costa Rica's stunning Pacific coast while exploring crocodilian habitats, coral restoration, and lush rainforest — a true coastal and jungle adventure for families.
content:
Set along Costa Rica's breathtaking Pacific Coast, this conservation project has been protecting endangered sea turtles and other vulnerable wildlife since 2009. Created by local scientists and community members, it combines biological research with hands-on action — and has contributed to the release of over 60,000 hatchlings.

As a volunteer, you will take part in beach night patrols between dusk and dawn, watching for nesting turtles and deterring poachers. During nesting season, you will help relocate eggs to a protected hatchery safe from predators and erosion. During hatching season, you will excavate nests, record data, and release hatchlings into the ocean.

Beyond turtles, the project offers an extraordinary range of conservation activities. You may monitor crocodilians and reptiles along the Térraba River, track mammals including monkeys, sloths, and anteaters through the jungle using camera traps, visit a coral restoration lab helping to rebuild bleached reefs in Marino Ballena National Park, and work in an on-site butterfly garden that breeds at-risk species like Monarchs.

Community education is central to the project — volunteers visit local schools, run workshops, and help children explore insect life cycles and the importance of conservation.

In your free time, families can enjoy surf lessons, horseback riding, zip-lining, hiking to waterfalls, whale watching (August–October), snorkelling, and diving.

The project runs year-round with arrivals every Monday. Accommodation, meals, and transfers from San José are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

title: Zimbabwe: Rhino & Elephant Conservation
description: A life-changing family volunteering experience at a private conservancy, working hands-on with endangered black and white rhinos and elephants in the heart of Zimbabwe.
content:
This family-run conservancy offers a unique opportunity to volunteer with endangered rhinos and elephants. As a volunteer, you will work alongside conservation experts on daily care of black and white rhinos and African elephants, carry out wildlife monitoring and behaviour observations, assist with anti-poaching patrols and conservancy management, educate local schoolchildren about conservation and the environment, and experience day-to-day life in rural Zimbabwe through meaningful community projects.

An optional horse-riding safari programme lets families explore the bush on horseback — locating animals, performing game counts, conducting snare patrols, and monitoring fences and boundaries from a unique elevated perspective.

Arrivals and departures are every Monday, with return transfers from Harare International Airport included. Accommodation, three meals a day, housekeeping, laundry, activities, and equipment are all provided. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

The conservancy plays a vital role in protecting and propagating endangered species to ensure viable wildlife populations continue to exist. Volunteering here gives families a behind-the-scenes understanding of what it truly takes to safeguard Africa's wildlife — a far deeper experience than ordinary travel.

title: Sri Lanka: Sea Turtle Conservation
description: Help protect endangered sea turtles along Sri Lanka's stunning southwestern coast — from burying rescued eggs and caring for hatchlings to releasing baby turtles into the ocean at dusk.
content:
Perched along the southwestern coast of Sri Lanka, this family-run turtle sanctuary offers a vital lifeline for the country's sea turtle populations. Despite legal protection, approximately only 1 in 1,000 hatchlings survive to adulthood due to predators, habitat loss, and human impact. Every nest, egg, and hatchling represents a critical link in the chain of survival for these vulnerable species.

The sanctuary sits on a stunning beach that is a vital nesting spot for olive ridley, green, and hawksbill turtles — all ranging from vulnerable to critically endangered. As a volunteer, you will contribute directly to increasing turtle survival rates and raising awareness in local communities about the importance of turtle conservation.

Daily activities include caring for the sanctuary's resident turtles by feeding them and cleaning tanks, carefully burying rescued eggs in protected hatcheries, and the highlight — releasing hatchlings into the sea at dusk when fewer predators are around. You will also help with regular beach clean-ups to remove plastic pollution and marine debris, and may have the opportunity to lead educational sanctuary tours for local visitors and teach English to schoolchildren.

The project runs year-round with arrivals every Monday. Accommodation, meals, airport transfers from Colombo, and all activities are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

This is a wholesome, hands-on conservation experience where your family can directly boost the number of hatchlings returning to the sea — and the very turtles you release could return to nest on these shores for decades to come.

title: Costa Rica: Sloth & Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Care for rescued sloths, monkeys, anteaters, and exotic birds at a rainforest wildlife sanctuary in Costa Rica — helping rehabilitate animals for release back into the wild.
content:
Deep in the Costa Rican rainforest, this wildlife sanctuary rescues, rehabilitates, and releases nearly 200 animals each year — including sloths, monkeys, anteaters, and exotic birds. Founded in 1999 by two young conservationists who began selling handmade crafts to fund rainforest protection, the sanctuary has grown into a vital hub for the region's wildlife.

As a volunteer, you will play a hands-on role in the daily care of the animals. Activities include preparing and distributing nutritious meals tailored to each species' dietary needs, creating enrichment activities that help rescued animals exercise natural instincts and build skills needed for survival in the wild, and keeping enclosures clean and maintained to excellent welfare standards.

You may also have the chance to witness animal rescues and releases first-hand — from rescuing a monkey that needs medical attention to releasing a rehabilitated sloth back into its forest home.

Beyond animal care, volunteers help with reforestation, general sanctuary maintenance, painting, gathering natural materials, and supporting the smooth running of the centre. One day a week you may visit the local marina for a meal by the ocean, and on your day off you can relax by the on-site pool, explore the local area, or try kayaking, parasailing, zip-lining, or visit a nearby national park.

The project runs year-round and families can join for as little as one week. Accommodation, meals, and airport transfers are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

This is a truly inspiring experience where your family can make a real difference to vulnerable wildlife while immersed in one of the most biodiverse countries on Earth.

title: Borneo: Orangutan & Rainforest Conservation
description: Explore the Bornean rainforest with your family — plant trees to restore orangutan habitat, cruise rivers teeming with wildlife, trek through ancient jungle, and live alongside an indigenous community.
content:
Journey to the Lower Kinabatangan Floodplain in Borneo — a WWF-protected 'Corridor of Life' that sustains some of the world's most extraordinary wildlife, from orangutans and pygmy elephants to proboscis monkeys, hornbills, and sun bears. Deforestation has devastated much of this habitat, and without intervention many species may not survive another generation.

As a family, you will help reforest depleted areas by learning to plant and maintain saplings on dedicated restoration sites. The trees you plant will grow to provide shelter and food for rainforest wildlife and create safe passageways through the corridor for animals to move freely.

Between conservation work, your family will embark on unforgettable river cruises through the heart of the rainforest, with an expert guide pointing out wildlife at every turn — in the trees, along the banks, and in the water below. You will also trek through magnificent ancient jungle, learning about the flora, fauna, and traditional medicinal plants used by local communities for generations.

A highlight of the experience is living alongside the Orang Sungai — the 'People of the River' — who will share their homes, stories, family traditions, and way of life with you. Your children will exchange cultural experiences, and you may be invited to join in traditional crafts, music, and dance. The trip concludes with a visit to a renowned orangutan rehabilitation centre, where you will witness feeding times and see these incredible great apes up close.

Accommodation, meals, guided activities, and transfers from Sandakan Airport are all included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

This is a truly immersive adventure that blends meaningful conservation work with extraordinary wildlife encounters and deep cultural exchange — an experience your family will never forget.

title: Namibia: Desert Elephant Conservation
description: A wild camping adventure in the Namib Desert — track elephant herds, camp under the stars, learn survival skills on bush walks, and help local communities coexist peacefully with these majestic animals.
content:
In the stunning drylands of the Namib Desert lives one of only two desert-dwelling elephant populations in the world. Reduced to just 300 in the 1980s, these herds are now growing — but with larger numbers comes greater demand for water and food, bringing elephants into conflict with local farming communities. Your family will play a crucial role in helping herds and villages coexist peacefully.

The adventure begins at a local primary school on the banks of the Ugab River, where your family will spend several days assisting with age-appropriate building projects and maintenance, interacting with pupils through play, arts and crafts, and lessons. This is a wonderful cultural exchange that encourages young minds to care about elephant conservation and leaves a lasting impact on the community.

From there, you will move to a bush base camp where nature walks with expert guides teach survival skills — which plants are edible, how to track wild animals on foot, and how to read the desert landscape. You may spot springbok, oryx, kudu, giraffe, zebra, and even critically endangered black rhino.

The highlight is several days of elephant patrols and tracking. Your family will pack up patrol vehicles and head into the desert to search for herds, recording data on births, deaths, movement patterns, and mating behaviour. Each night you will set up camp wherever the elephants lead you, sleeping under a blanket of stars and drifting off to the sounds of the Namibian night.

Accommodation ranges from a riverside school camp and a treehouse base camp to wild camping during patrols. Meals and transfers from Swakopmund are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

This is the ultimate outdoor family adventure — combining meaningful conservation work with extraordinary wildlife encounters, cultural exchange, and the magic of sleeping under African skies.

title: Sri Lanka: Elephant Conservation & Community
description: Help protect Asiatic elephants on the edge of a national park in Sri Lanka — monitor herds, gather vital research data, repair homes damaged by human-elephant conflict, and teach English in local schools.
content:
Based on the outskirts of a stunning national park in central Sri Lanka, this conservation project works to protect Asiatic elephants and reduce human-elephant conflict. In the last century, approximately 90% of Sri Lanka's elephant population has disappeared, with around 200 elephants and 80 people still lost each year due to conflict between communities and herds.

As a volunteer, you will spend afternoons and evenings in a jeep along the 'elephant corridor', watching for herds to emerge and gathering data on their size, sex, and physical features. This information helps the project monitor populations and predict areas of potential conflict. You will also complete trail transects to locate and analyse elephant dung — revealing age, size, gender, eating patterns, and movement.

Mornings are devoted to species monitoring using camera traps, GPS tracking, remote sensors, and bird-mapping surveys to assess the overall health of the forest ecosystem. You may spot leopards, sloth bears, wild boar, deer, and a wealth of bird species. A trip to the nearby national park offers an unforgettable safari experience.

The project has pioneered innovative solutions to human-elephant conflict, including planting citrus trees around villages to deter elephants while creating a sustainable income for residents. Volunteers help monitor these systems and may assist with repairing homes, wells, and food stores damaged by elephant raids. A free 'Elebus' service safely transports children through elephant corridors to school — and you may help with the school run.

Three mornings a week, volunteers teach English at local schools, working with children from primary age through to teenagers, helping them understand both the language and the importance of elephant conservation.

Weekends are free to explore Sri Lanka's cultural triangle, ancient World Heritage sites, or simply relax in the stunning surroundings.

Accommodation, meals, and airport transfers are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

title: Peru: Amazon Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Live in the heart of the Amazon Rainforest and help rehabilitate rescued wildlife — from manatees and monkeys to wild cats and sloths — while searching for pink river dolphins and exploring ancient indigenous cultures.
content:
Deep in the Peruvian Amazon — the second-largest expanse of rainforest on Earth — this wildlife sanctuary works in collaboration with local authorities to rescue, rehabilitate, and release native species. From gentle Amazonian manatees and playful monkeys to agile wild cats and charming sloths, the sanctuary provides a safe haven for animals rescued from poaching, habitat loss, and the illegal wildlife trade.

As a volunteer, you will play a hands-on role in the daily care of the animals. You will prepare species-specific meals in the sanctuary kitchen — meat for carnivores, fruits and vegetables for herbivores, and milk bottles for babies. You will design and build creative enrichment activities that stimulate natural behaviours and prepare animals for release. You will observe and monitor wildlife behaviour, contributing vital data that guides rehabilitation and care strategies.

Sanctuary maintenance is equally important — cleaning enclosures, repairing fences, remodelling habitats, and ensuring every animal enjoys the best possible quality of life.

Community outreach is at the heart of the project. Weekly classes blend environmental education with English, art, and science for local children, inspiring the next generation of environmental ambassadors. Volunteers may also join campaigns in the wider community, helping develop sustainable ways for people to coexist with the rainforest.

A highlight is a boat ride along the Amazon River in search of pink river dolphins — one of only four river dolphin species in the world. Longer stays unlock extraordinary experiences: a trek through the Allpahuayo Mishana National Reserve with its world-record biodiversity, and a visit to the Maloca Kukama Tribe for traditional face painting, dancing, and cultural exchange.

In your free time, hike to a creek, float across a serene lake inhabited by rehabilitated manatees and giant Arapaima fish, or organise day adventures with the sanctuary team.

Accommodation, meals, and airport transfers from Iquitos are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

title: Zimbabwe: Wildlife Conservation
description: Live on a 3,000-acre private game reserve in the heart of Zimbabwe, combining hands-on wildlife conservation with horseback safaris, elephant encounters, and community education.
content:
Set on a vast 3,000-acre private game reserve in Zimbabwe's Midlands Province, this extraordinary project blends hands-on wildlife conservation with the thrill of horseback safaris and deeply rewarding community work.

The reserve is home to an incredible diversity of African wildlife — zebra, wildebeest, giraffes, impala, kudu, and over 200 bird species roam freely across the open bushveld. The project also cares for lions, elephants, and rhinos as part of dedicated conservation programmes.

As a volunteer, your days are rich and varied. You will walk alongside elephants through the African bush, learning about their behaviour and the challenges they face. You will monitor rhinos on foot — standing just metres from these magnificent animals — recording vital data that supports anti-poaching efforts. Lion enrichment sessions let you observe and contribute to the welfare of resident big cats.

What sets this project apart is its remarkable safari stables programme. Whether you are an experienced rider or a complete beginner, you can enjoy horseback safaris riding alongside giraffes, zebras, and wildebeest. Sunrise rides across the open bush, horse swims, polocrosse, showjumping, and cross-country are all on offer. The stables also run a horse therapy programme for local children with disabilities — a deeply moving experience for volunteers and families alike.

Evening game drives offer the chance to spot nocturnal wildlife, and bonfire nights under the vast African sky are a highlight of the social calendar.

Community work is central to the experience. You will visit local schools to teach English, maths, and life skills, support school infrastructure projects, and connect with children and families in the surrounding area.

Accommodation is in authentic African river tents with private balconies overlooking the bush. Full board meals, a swimming pool, laundry service, WiFi, and all project activities with professional guides are included. Families simply need to arrange flights, travel insurance, and visa fees.

With wildlife on your doorstep, horses in the stables, and a community that welcomes you with open arms, this is an African adventure unlike any other.
